Shabbat Parshat Teitzei,

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the verse "Rejoice, make glad the beloved friends" and questions why joy is needed in Chochmah and Binah if Binah is inherently joyful and Chochmah contains pleasure beyond joy.

translations.translation: "Rejoice, make glad the beloved friends, as You gladdened Your creation in the Garden of Eden from before."
And it is explained in this discourse
(which was said at the wedding of the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, on the day of Shabbat Kodesh,
that "the beloved friends" refer to the level of Chochmah and Binah, which are called "the two friends that never part,"
and the request "Rejoice, make glad the beloved friends" is that joy should be drawn into Chochmah and Binah.
And it needs to be understood,
for Binah is the place of joy, as it is written,
"The mother of the children is joyful,"
and it is known
that "the mother of the children" refers to Binah, which is the mother that gives birth to the emotions,
and as is also seen tangibly, that when a person comprehends something with his intellect, he has joy from it,
and also in Chochmah, where joy does not apply,
because joy is specifically from revelation, and Chochmah
(like a flashing bolt of lightning)
is above revelation,
yet in Chochmah, the revelation of pleasure shines,
as in "the face of Rabbi Abahu shone"
when he found a new Tosefta,
for the shining of the face is from the revelation of pleasure,
and it is known that pleasure is above joy,
so what is the request "Rejoice, make glad the beloved friends,"
since there is already joy in Binah,
and certainly in Chochmah, which contains pleasure that is above joy?
And also it needs to be understood,
for "the beloved friends"
(simply)
refer to the groom and bride,
and it is known that the groom and bride are Zeir Anpin and Nukvah,
and what is the connection of this interpretation
(that "the beloved friends" refer to the groom and bride,
Zeir Anpin and Nukvah)
with the aforementioned interpretation that "friends"
("the beloved")
are Chochmah and Binah?

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the connection between the two interpretations of "beloved friends" by stating that Zeir Anpin and Nukvah are included in Chochmah and Binah and later resemble them, using the gematria of "ahuvim" (beloved) equaling "dodim" (lovers).

translations.translation: B)
And it can be said that this will be understood
(the connection between the two interpretations)
based on what is written in the book Emet L'Yaakov
(cited in the aforementioned discourse)
that "ahuvim" (beloved) in gematria equals "dodim" (lovers), and they are Zeir Anpin and Nukvah
(and as is known,
"friends" are Chochmah and Binah, and "lovers" are Zeir Anpin and Nukvah).
And what is written "the beloved friends,"
the word "beloved" is a continuation and description of "friends," which refers
(as above)
to Chochmah and Binah,
can be explained in two ways.
First,
based on what is known
about the manner of the birth of the emotions
(Zeir Anpin and Nukvah)
from the intellect
(Chochmah and Binah),
that initially they are included within the intellect, and afterward they are drawn forth in revelation.
And based on this, it can be said,
that "the beloved friends" refers to Zeir Anpin and Nukvah
("beloved")
as they are included within Chochmah and Binah
("friends"),
unlike "beloved"
(simply)
which refers to Zeir Anpin and Nukvah as they are drawn forth in revelation,
"beloved" in gematria equals "lovers."
And based on this, it will also be understood that the matter of Zeir Anpin and Nukvah
("lovers")
is hinted at in the gematria of "beloved"
("beloved" in gematria equals "lovers"),
for gematria indicates a diminution of light and vitality, diminution after diminution,
because the drawing down from the emotions that are in the intellect
("the beloved friends")
to the emotions that are in the heart
("beloved" in gematria equals "lovers")
is through several contractions.
And second,
that since the emotions are offspring of the intellect,
for Chochmah and Binah are father and mother, and Zeir Anpin and Nukvah are son and daughter
[as it is stated in Kabbalah
that father and mother are Yud-Hei
(Chochmah and Binah),
and son and daughter are Vav-Hei
(Zeir Anpin and Nukvah)],
they resemble the intellect
(even after they have been drawn forth and revealed),
for the father bequeaths to his son, etc., to the point that the heir is in the place of the one who bequeaths,
and likewise regarding the daughter
(when she inherits,
in a place where there is no son)
[and in particular,
the son is in the place of the father,
and the daughter is in the place of the mother, as it is written,
"Like mother, like daughter"].
Therefore, based on this, it can be said,
that even after they have been drawn forth and revealed,
they are called by the name "the beloved friends"
(and as above,
that "the beloved friends" simply refers to the groom and bride,
Zeir Anpin and Nukvah in revelation),
because even then
(after their drawing down and revelation)
they resemble Chochmah and Binah.
